content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route up to 5 steps, leaves must be commercially available, total price <= $9999. Need to output JSON tree.

We have a target molecule: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O

Looks like a polyunsaturated fatty acid derivative with a cyclic acetal? Actually it's a cyclic diol (maybe a sugar) attached to a polyene chain ending with carboxylic acid.

We have a template (38653) that breaks an ether forming a double bond: retro: [C:1]/[CH]=[CH]/[C:4] >> [C:1]-[C@@H]1-O-[C@H]1-[C:4] (i.e., forms a cyclic acetal from a double bond). Applying to target gave two possible precursors: both are similar: C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/[C@@H]2O[C@H]2C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO and another with different geometry.

So the disconnection suggests the target can be formed by a cyclization (intramolecular ether formation) from a linear precursor containing a double bond and a hydroxyl group.

Thus we can propose a retrosynthetic step: target -> linear precursor (call it A). Then we need to break further.

The linear precursor appears to be a polyene chain with a terminal carboxylic acid and a primary alcohol (CO). Actually the precursor SMILES: C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/[C@@H]2O[C@H]2C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO

Let's analyze: It has a terminal primary alcohol (CO) attached to the double bond carbon (allylic alcohol). Also contains a cyclic acetal? Wait it still has O[C@@H]... Actually the precursor still contains a cyclic acetal? It has O[C@@H](C/C=C/[C@@H]2O[C@H]2C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C. That's a tetrahydrofuran ring? Actually O[C@@H]... maybe a 5-membered cyclic ether (tetrahydrofuran) attached to a side chain.

But the template suggests the cyclic acetal is formed from a double bond and an alcohol. So the precursor still has a double bond and an alcohol that will cyclize.

Thus next step: break the double bond to form a simpler chain.

We can search for templates that break C=C to give carbonyls or other groups.

Let's search for functional groups broken: C-C double bonds.
